draft.title: How texts build a theme
card: A theme is rarely stated outright. It grows from patterns that a reader notices across a whole text.
Repeated images
the same object, colour or setting turns up again and again. For example, a story where a locked gate appears in many scenes keeps pointing to the idea of being shut out.
Contrasts
two characters are set against each other. If one shares and the other hoards, the reader sees which choice the text values.
Ending
what happens at the end shows the result of the choices made. It often suggests the idea the text wants the reader to take away.
draft.remember: To support a claim about theme, trace a pattern through the text and explain what it suggests.

a.q: In a story, Kai's torch is shown in the opening, the middle and the final scene, each time lighting a path for someone else. What is this an example of?
opts: A repeated image that builds a theme
A contrast between two characters
An ending that solves the problem
A subject stated outright by the writer
a.why: The torch returns in several scenes, so it forms a pattern of repeated images. A contrast needs two characters set against each other, and the torch is one object that appears again and again.
a.clue: Look at what keeps coming back across the story.

b.q: Priya wants to support her claim that a novel is about the cost of pride. Which of these would best support it?
opts: Tracing how the proud character keeps losing friends
Stating that the novel has a lot of characters in it
Retelling the plot from start to finish in order
Saying that she enjoyed reading the novel very much
b.why: A theme claim is supported by tracing a pattern, such as the proud character losing something again and again. Retelling the plot only says what happens and does not show a pattern or what it suggests.
b.clue: Which answer follows a pattern through the text?

a.best: A repeated image that builds a theme

b.best: Tracing how the proud character keeps losing friends

problems.detail: The stem says Priya claims the novel 'is about the cost of pride'. Point 1 of this chapter defines the subject as what a text is about and the theme as an idea written as a sentence. This phrasing blurs the two. Something like 'her claim that the novel suggests pride can cost a person their friendships' would match how the chapter frames a theme.

b.q: Priya claims that a novel suggests pride can cost a person their friendships. Which of these would best support her claim?
opts: Tracing how the proud character loses friend after friend
Pointing to one scene where the proud character boasts
Retelling the plot of the novel from start to finish
Counting how many friendships appear in the novel
b.why: A claim about theme is supported by tracing a pattern, such as the proud character losing friends again and again. One boastful scene shows pride only once, so it is not a pattern and does not show what pride costs.
b.clue: Which answer follows something through the whole text?
